name: Diodeline
tagline: Tech news, traced to the source.
positioning: Diodeline is the tech newsroom that turns launch-day noise into dated briefings, versioned explainers and spec cards that print the fine print, so readers know what a claim actually depends on.
audience: Curious, busy gadget owners and early-career tech professionals (24-45) who want to decide whether to update, upgrade or wait without wading through hype.
strategy: Own clarity over speed: every story is dated, every explainer is versioned, and every spec claim carries its condition. A running changelog and a weekday email build a habit, while social turns the method itself (spec cards, launch anatomy, Ask the Desk) into save-worthy, shareable formats.

contrastPairs.use: body text and headlines on light
labels on green chips and buttons

designSystem.spacing: 8px base grid; section padding 56-96px; 16-40px fluid gutters; 18px card gaps.
designSystem.radius: Tight 6px for cards, chips and buttons; 12-20px for dark 'board' panels; full pills only for filters.
designSystem.borders: 1px cool-grey hairlines (#D9DDE7); 2px ink rules under section heads; 4px violet left-border on lead stories; dashed rules for 'why it matters'.
designSystem.imagery: Original inline SVG only: circuit boards, chip packages, device line-drawings and diagrams on dot-grid substrates. No photos.
designSystem.shapes: Diode triangle-and-bar, right-angled circuit traces with 45-degree jogs, round solder nodes, rectangular version tags.
designSystem.buttons: Solid violet primary with white text, ink outline ghost, green 'terminal' submit; mono arrow glyph (->) as affordance.
designSystem.cards: White briefing cards with SAMPLE STORY + category + date chips, a headline, summary and a dashed 'Why it matters' footer; dark spec cards pair a device drawing with a claim/condition table.
designSystem.motifs: Diode/arrow logo, circuit traces, version-tag chips (v4.0, fw 2.6.1), product spec cards, vertical changelog rails with nodes.

artDirection: Compose every piece like a circuit board: a dark substrate or a light cleanroom grid, with one signal-green trace carrying the eye from the headline to the evidence. Headlines are heavy Red Hat Display set tight, with violet reserved for the key word; all metadata (dates, versions, SAMPLE labels) lives in Red Hat Mono chips. Each asset shows the method, not hype: spec claims always appear with their condition, and timelines read like changelogs. Keep one diode mark visible, generous 64px+ margins and no more than one accent colour per focal point.
